what: Labcorp runs clinical laboratories. It processes blood and other samples ordered by doctors and hospitals, and also runs a central laboratory business supporting pharmaceutical clinical trials.
customers: Doctors, hospitals and health systems ordering tests, insurers and patients paying for them, and drug companies running trials.
money: central laboratory and early development services for drug trials
moat: A national network of laboratories and collection sites with contracts with insurers, where volume drives down cost per test below what smaller labs can achieve.
risks: Reimbursement rates for routine tests are under continual government pressure
Net margin of about 6% is thin
Debt of about $7 billion against almost no cash
opportunities: Hospitals outsourcing their laboratories to it adds volume without new facilities
Specialty testing in oncology and neurology earns far more per test than routine work
watch: Organic test volume growth and revenue per test.
